title: Attention-Like Hebbian Learning from Quantum Probability Flow and Quantum-Annealer Tests
summary: We propose a quantum probability-flow principle for deriving local learning rules in associative memory. A transverse field defines leakage channels from data states, and minimizing the measured survival loss gives stability-driven updates. For imaginary-time, dephased dynamics, the local leakage free energy is the log-sum-exp of energy gaps; its gradient is a softmax-weighted Hebbian rule. Real-time stability instead yields a power-law weighting. D-Wave standard- and fast-anneal tests of a one-hot attention forward map are better fitted by an effective softmax than by a Lorentzian power law.
